lessons.culture: Iraqis open a catch-up with شلونك or شكو ماكو, and البارحة is the everyday word for yesterday. When someone had a hard day you say يا حرام for sympathy or الله يعينك (God help you).

exercises.prompt: صديقك يسألك: "شسويت البارحة؟". جاوبه إنك رحت للسوگ.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic, but far too formal for a chat; Baghdadis say رحت للسوگ and البارحة.

exercises.prompt: يسألوك: "وين چنت البارحة بالليل؟". جاوب إنك چنت بالبيت.

too_formal.feedback: في المنزل is formal; in Baghdad it is بالبيت, and كنت is said چنت.

exercises.tip: چنت = I was; the ch sound replaces k, as in چان.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ چان يوم طويل مرة." المعنى: Yesterday was a very long day.

too_formal.feedback: أمس is the written word; spoken Iraqi says البارحة.

exercises.tip: البارحة opens the sentence, like "yesterday" in English.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "تعبت مرة من _____ البارحة." المعنى: I got very tired from work yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: العمل is correct but bookish; the everyday word for work is الشغل.

exercises.tip: مرة after a verb means "very", not "once".

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "What did you do yesterday?" (تحچي وياه، رجال)

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; spoken Iraqi squeezes "what did you do" into شسويت.

exercises.tip: شسويت = شنو + سويت, what you did.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who did you see yesterday?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; Iraqis say منو for who and شفت for saw.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "I bought something yesterday"؟

too_formal.feedback: Fine as written Arabic, but شريت and شي are what is said day to day.

exercises.tip: A past-tense verb plus البارحة marks something already done.

exercises.prompt: شنو معنى "لأي ساعة سهرت البارحة؟"؟

exercises.tip: سهر = to stay up late in the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: هلا سارة، شلونچ؟ شنو دتسوين؟
dialogue.transliteration: hala saara, shloonich? shinu datsawwiin?
dialogue.english: Hi Sara, how are you? What are you up to?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: هلا مصطفى، دا أفتكر أيام زمان. لمن چنت صغيرة چنت أحب ألعب برة
dialogue.transliteration: hala mustafa, da aftikir ayyaam zamaan. lamma chint sagheera chint a7ibb al3ab barra
dialogue.english: Hi Mustafa, I'm remembering the old days. When I was little I loved to play outside.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: وين كبرتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: ween kibarti?
dialogue.english: Where did you grow up?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: كبرت بمحلة گديمة ببغداد، بالكرخ
dialogue.transliteration: kibart b-ma7alla gdeema b-baghdaad, bil-karkh
dialogue.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Baghdad, in Karkh.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: وآني هم، چان عندي رفيگ اسمه كريم
dialogue.transliteration: w-aani hamm, chaan 3indi rafeeg ismah kareem
dialogue.english: Me too, I had a friend named Kareem.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: شنو چنتوا تسوون وياه؟
dialogue.transliteration: shinu chintu tsawwoon wiyyaah?
dialogue.english: What did you used to do with him?

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: چنا نلعب طوبة بالزگاگ، وكل يوم نروح للمدرسة مشي سوية
dialogue.transliteration: chinna nil3ab 6ooba biz-zugaag, w-kull yoom nirooh lil-madrasa mashi sawiyya
dialogue.english: We used to play football in the alley, and every day we went to school on foot together.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: آني چنت أخاف مرة من الظلمة، وستي چانت تحچيلنا حچايات گبل النوم
dialogue.transliteration: aani chint akhaaf marra min iz-zilma, w-sitti chaanat ti7chiilna 7chaayaat gabil in-noom
dialogue.english: I was very afraid of the dark, and my grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: الله! وكل صيف چنا نروح لجدي بالريف
dialogue.transliteration: allah! w-kull seef chinna nirooh l-jiddi bir-reef
dialogue.english: Oh! And every summer we used to go to my grandfather's in the village.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: وكتها الحياة چانت أبسط هواية
dialogue.transliteration: wakitha il-7ayaa chaanat absa6 hawaaya
dialogue.english: Back then life was much simpler.

dialogue.speaker: Mustafa
dialogue.arabic: صح، وآني چنت أحلم أصير طيار
dialogue.transliteration: sa7, w-aani chint a7lam aseer 6ayyaar
dialogue.english: True, and I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: وآني چنت أحلم أصير معلمة. المهم، الحمد لله على كل شي
dialogue.transliteration: w-aani chint a7lam aseer mu3allima. il-muhimm, il-7amdulillah 3ala kull shi
dialogue.english: And I dreamed of becoming a teacher. Anyway, praise God for everything.

lessons.culture: Iraqis often tell childhood stories about the old محلة, football in the زگاگ and summers at the grandparents' place in the countryside. ستي and جدي are the warm everyday words for grandmother and grandfather, and أيام زمان (the old days) opens most such stories.

exercises.tip: چنا + present verb = we used to do it.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: هلا نور، شلونچ؟
dialogue.transliteration: hala noor, shloonich?
dialogue.english: Hi Noor, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: هلا أحمد، شبيك؟ وجهك تعبان
dialogue.transliteration: hala a7mad, shbeek? wijhak ta3baan
dialogue.english: Hi Ahmed, what's wrong? You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: أوف، البارحة كلشي خربان. موبايلي انكسر
dialogue.transliteration: oof, il-baar7a kullshi kharbaan. mobaayli inkisar
dialogue.english: Ugh, yesterday everything went wrong. My phone broke.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: يا ساتر! وشلون انكسر؟
dialogue.transliteration: ya saatir! w-shloon inkisar?
dialogue.english: God protect us! And how did it break?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: وگع مني بالدرج، وآني هم وگعت وتعورت برجلي
dialogue.transliteration: wiga3 minni bid-daraj, w-aani hamm wiga3it w-ta3awwarit b-rijli
dialogue.english: It fell out of my hand on the stairs, and I fell too and hurt my leg.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: الله يشافيك! هسة رجلك زينة؟
dialogue.transliteration: allah yshaafeek! hassa rijlak zeena?
dialogue.english: God heal you! Is your leg okay now?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: أحسن شوية. وبعدين ضيعت چليد البيت ونسيت الجزدان بالبيت
dialogue.transliteration: a7san shwayya. w-ba3deen dayya3it chleed il-beet w-niseet ij-juzdaan bil-beet
dialogue.english: A bit better. And then I lost the house key and forgot my wallet at home.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله! وشلون دخلت للبيت؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa 7awla wa laa quwwata illa billaah! w-shloon dakhalit lil-beet?
dialogue.english: There is no power or strength except with God! And how did you get into the house?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: أخوي جه وفتح الباب، وبعدين الكهرباء طفت كل الليل
dialogue.transliteration: akhooy ja w-fata7 il-baab, w-ba3deen ik-kahraba 6ufat kull il-leel
dialogue.english: My brother came and opened the door, and then the power went out all night.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: وهاي الصبح شصار؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-haay is-sub7 shsaar?
dialogue.english: And this morning, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: نمت هواية وما سمعت المنبه، وتأخرت عالدوام
dialogue.transliteration: nimit hawaaya w-ma sma3it il-munabbih, w-ta2akhkhart 3ad-dawaam
dialogue.english: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm, and I was late for work.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: معليش، إن شاء الله اليوم أحسن
dialogue.transliteration: ma3leesh, in shaa2 allah il-yoom a7san
dialogue.english: Never mind, God willing today is better.

lessons.culture: When something goes wrong Iraqis answer with يا ساتر or الله يشافيك and end the story with الحمد لله على كل حال. Power cuts (الكهرباء طفت) are such an ordinary complaint in Iraq that they come up in casual talk all the time.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: هلا عمر، ماكو شي جديد، الحمد لله. وأنت؟
dialogue.transliteration: hala 3umar, maaku shi jideed, il-7amdulillah. w-inta?
dialogue.english: Hi Omar, nothing new, thank God. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: عندي خبر ما راح تصدگينه. سمعت سامر خطب
dialogue.transliteration: 3indi khabar ma raa7 tsaddigeena. sma3it saamer kha6ab
dialogue.english: I have news you won't believe. I heard Samer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: صدگ؟ منو گال لك هالخبر؟
dialogue.transliteration: sidig? minu gaal-lak hal-khabar?
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you this news?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أمي گالتلي، وهي سمعتها من خالتي
dialogue.transliteration: ummi gaaltilli, w-hiyya sma3atha min khaalti
dialogue.english: My mother told me, and she heard it from my aunt.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: لا تصدگين كلشي، يمكن بس إشاعة. بعدنا ما متأكدين
dialogue.transliteration: laa tsaddigeen kullshi, yimkin bass ishaa3a. ba3dna ma mit2akkideen
dialogue.english: Don't believe everything, it might just be a rumor. We're not sure yet.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لا، هاي مو إشاعة. وأختي تزوجت الشهر اللي فات، تعرفين؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa, haay mu ishaa3a. w-ukhti tzawwijat ish-shahr illi faat, ti3rifeen?
dialogue.english: No, it's not a rumor. And my sister got married last month, you know?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: مبروك لأختك! وسمعنا صار عندهم ولد جيراننا
dialogue.transliteration: mabrook li-ukhtak! w-smi3na saar 3ind-hum walad jiiraanna
dialogue.english: Congratulations to your sister! And we heard our neighbors had a baby boy.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: الله يخليه لهم. وسمعت يگولون محل أبو علي سكّر
dialogue.transliteration: allah ykhalleeh la-hum. w-sma3it ygoolun ma7all abu 3ali sakkar
dialogue.english: May God keep him for them. And I heard they're saying Abu Ali's shop closed.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: ما أدري، هاي كلها حچي ناس
dialogue.transliteration: ma adri, haay kullha 7chi naas
dialogue.english: I don't know, that's all just people's talk.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: صح. وگبل ما أنسى، لا تگولين لأحد، بس سمعت راح يسافرون
dialogue.transliteration: sa7. w-gabil ma ansa, laa tguuleen la-a7ad, bass sma3it raa7 ysaafrun
dialogue.english: True. And before I forget, don't tell anyone, but I heard they're going to travel.

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: لا تخاف، سر عندي. الله يوفقهم
dialogue.transliteration: laa tkhaaf, sirr 3indi. allah ywaffigehum
dialogue.english: Don't worry, my lips are sealed. May God grant them success.

pair.english: Is this true or a rumor?

lessons.culture: News in Iraq travels through family and neighbors, and شكو ماكو (what is there, what isn't) is the classic opener. Gossip is softened with هاي حچي ناس, and good news is met with مبروك at engagements, weddings and births.

exercises.prompt: صديقك يسألك: "شكو ماكو؟". جاوبه إن ماكو شي جديد.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; Iraqis say ماكو for there isn't.

exercises.tip: ماكو = there is none; شكو = what is there.

exercises.prompt: يسألوك: "منو گال لك هالخبر؟". جاوب إن أمك گالتلك.

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; گالتلي (she told me) is the spoken form.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ محل فلان سكّر." المعنى: They're saying that such-and-such shop closed.

too_formal.feedback: يُقال إن is written style; spoken Iraqi uses يگولون.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "أختي _____ الشهر اللي فات." المعنى: My sister got married last month.

too_formal.feedback: عقدت قرانها is formal and written; people say تزوجت.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who told you this news?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; spoken Iraqi is منو گال لك هالخبر.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "What's the latest news with you?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; شكو ماكو is the everyday Iraqi way to ask what's new.

exercises.tip: شكو ماكو is a greeting as much as a question.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "We heard they had a baby boy"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; spoken Iraqi says صار عندهم ولد.

exercises.prompt: شنو معنى "هاي كلها حچي ناس"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; حچي ناس is the spoken way.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: ما خبر راح عندي تصدگه

too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; spoken Iraqi uses ما راح for will not.

exercises.tip: راح before a verb marks the future.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: أحد بس تگول راح لا سمعت يسافرون لأ
exercises.answer: لا تگول لأحد بس سمعت راح يسافرون
accepted: لا تگول لأحد بس سمعت راح يسافرون
laa tguul la-a7ad bass sma3it raa7 ysaafrun
لا تگول لأحد، بس سمعت راح يسافرون

too_formal.item: لا تخبر أحداً لكني سمعت أنهم سيسافرون
too_formal.feedback: Correct written Arabic; spoken Iraqi is لا تگول لأحد.

challenge.title: Tell Me What Happened
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Iraqi conversation of at least 10 lines between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer in the past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using البارحة and شسويت or شصار.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using لمن چنت صغير or چنا.
Something that went wrong, using a word like انكسر, ضيعت, or تأخرت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت or گالولي.
At least one masculine-address form such as شفت or چنت.
At least one feminine-address form such as شسويتي or چنتي.
A closing reaction such as يا حرام, يا ساتر, or معليش.

dialogue.speaker: Basim
dialogue.arabic: هلا نور، شلونچ؟ شسويتي البارحة؟
dialogue.transliteration: hala noor, shloonich? shsawweeti il-baar7a?
dialogue.english: Hi Noor, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: هلا باسم، زينة الحمد لله. البارحة رحت للسوگ، بس موبايلي انكسر
dialogue.transliteration: hala baasim, zeena il-7amdulillah. il-baar7a ru7t lis-soog, bass mobaayli inkisar
dialogue.english: Hi Basim, good, thank God. Yesterday I went to the market, but my phone broke.

dialogue.speaker: Basim
dialogue.arabic: يا ساتر! وشلون انكسر؟
dialogue.transliteration: ya saatir! w-shloon inkisar?
dialogue.english: God protect us! How did it break?

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: وگع مني بالدرج. المهم، شكو ماكو عندك؟
dialogue.transliteration: wiga3 minni bid-daraj. il-muhimm, shaku maaku 3indak?
dialogue.english: It fell from my hand on the stairs. Anyway, what's new with you?

dialogue.speaker: Basim
dialogue.arabic: سمعت سامر خطب، بس بعدنا ما متأكدين
dialogue.transliteration: sma3it saamer kha6ab, bass ba3dna ma mit2akkideen
dialogue.english: I heard Samer got engaged, but we're not sure yet.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: مبروك إذا صحيح! آني چنت أفتكر أيام زمان، چنا نلعب طوبة بالزگاگ
dialogue.transliteration: mabrook idha sa7ee7! aani chint aftikir ayyaam zamaan, chinna nil3ab 6ooba biz-zugaag
dialogue.english: Congratulations if true! I was remembering the old days, we used to play football in the alley.

dialogue.speaker: Basim
dialogue.arabic: وآني هم، لمن چنت صغير چنت أحلم أصير طيار
dialogue.transliteration: w-aani hamm, lamma chint sagheer chint a7lam aseer 6ayyaar
dialogue.english: Me too, when I was young I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: وأنت ليش ما جيت البارحة؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-inta leesh ma jeet il-baar7a?
dialogue.english: And you, why didn't you come yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Basim
dialogue.arabic: نمت هواية وما سمعت المنبه، آسف
dialogue.transliteration: nimit hawaaya w-ma sma3it il-munabbih, aasif
dialogue.english: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm, sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Noor
dialogue.arabic: معليش، إن شاء الله باچر نشوفك
dialogue.transliteration: ma3leesh, in shaa2 allah baachir nshoofak
dialogue.english: Never mind, God willing we'll see you tomorrow.
